title: Functional Network Overlay Atlas
subtitle: Overlay default-mode, salience, executive, dorsal-attention and sensorimotor systems
altText: Interactive chalkboard-style anatomical map of Functional Network Overlay Atlas with selectable regions and pathways.
learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Functional Network Overlay Atlas.
Trace key inputs, outputs and connections in the Functional Network Overlay Atlas.
Interpret lesion patterns cautiously using distributed-network and clinical context.

sections.explainSimply: Overlay default-mode, salience, executive, dorsal-attention and sensorimotor systems.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Network models fit transdiagnostic formulation better than single-region explanations, but resting-state correlations are not direct measures of thoughts or diagnoses.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Location: Large-scale networks span noncontiguous cortical and subcortical nodes, often overlapping within hub regions. Major subdivisions include default mode network, salience network, frontoparietal control network, dorsal attention network, ventral attention network, sensorimotor network, visual network, limbic network. Inputs include sensory systems, interoceptive signals, memory systems, task goals, reward and threat signals; outputs include motor systems, autonomic systems, memory updating, attention allocation, goal-directed behaviour.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A dynamic transport and control map: the meaning of any node depends on the routes entering, leaving and bypassing it.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Network models fit transdiagnostic formulation better than single-region explanations, but resting-state correlations are not direct measures of thoughts or diagnoses.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Damage or dysconnectivity may disturb attention, self-related thought, executive control, awareness or behaviour. Similar symptoms can arise from different nodes, and one lesion can affect several networks.
sections.clinicalPearl: Ask which network should dominate for the task, which network should disengage, and whether switching between them is efficient.
sections.practicalExample: Select a region, trace its incoming and outgoing pathways, then compare healthy and lesion overlays before forming a clinical hypothesis.
sections.limitationsCautions: Network boundaries depend on analytic method, task, arousal and individual variability. Functional connectivity is statistical dependence, not proof of direct anatomical connection or causal influence.

anatomy.position: Large-scale networks span noncontiguous cortical and subcortical nodes, often overlapping within hub regions.
anatomy.spatialRelationships: Interpreted relative to connected cortical, subcortical and vascular structures; boundaries and laterality must be checked in the selected view.
anatomy.bloodSupply: Network nodes cross multiple arterial territories, so vascular lesions may fragment a network at one or several points.
anatomy.lesionEffects: Damage or dysconnectivity may disturb attention, self-related thought, executive control, awareness or behaviour. Similar symptoms can arise from different nodes, and one lesion can affect several networks.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Network models fit transdiagnostic formulation better than single-region explanations, but resting-state correlations are not direct measures of thoughts or diagnoses.

quiz.question: Which network is most associated with detecting behaviourally relevant internal and external events and coordinating switching?
quiz.rationale: The salience network, particularly anterior insula and dorsal anterior cingulate regions, is implicated in relevance detection and network switching.

quiz.question: Functional connectivity means:
options: Statistical dependence between signals over time
quiz.rationale: Functional connectivity is correlational and does not by itself establish direct structural connection or causality.

quiz.question: Why can one focal lesion affect several cognitive domains?
options: Hub regions and shared pathways participate in multiple networks
Each region performs exactly one function
quiz.rationale: Connector hubs and overlapping systems allow focal damage to propagate effects across multiple networks.
